jobs.description: Job Search Subscribe to jobs Assistant Professor - Department of Primary Care, Division of Osteopathic Manual Medicine (OMM) Apply now Job no: 492994 Work type: FT Location: Des Moines Categories: Clinical Faculty and Staff Des Moines University Medicine and Health Sciences is seeking a clinically focused, mission-driven physician educator to join the Division of Osteopathic Manual Medicine (OMM). This role offers a unique opportunity to build a meaningful clinical practice while shaping the next generation of physicians through hands-on teaching and mentorship. The position is primarily dedicated to delivering high-quality primary care, including osteopathic manual medicine, complemented by a defined and impactful commitment to academic engagement. What you’ll do: Provide comprehensive primary care, integrating osteopathic manual medicine, while managing an active patient panel and supporting clinic operations Meet clinical productivity and quality benchmarks; participate in peer review and quality improvement initiatives Precept medical students in clinical settings and mentor OMM scholars and residents Contribute to teaching across lectures, labs, and clinical instruction, including student evaluation and assessment Engage in service activities, including committees, admissions, community outreach, and required compliance responsibilities What we are looking for: Have earned a Doctor of Osteopathy or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine degree from an AOA-accredited college of osteopathic medicine. Board-eligible/certified by the American Osteopathic Board of (specialty) or board-eligible/certified by the American Board of (specialty). If board-eligible, you must obtain certification within one year of employment. Must possess significant experience in osteopathic manual medicine (e.g. completion of an undergraduate OMM fellowship/scholarship, experience teaching OMM, completion of an OMM/NMM residency, etc.) Be a member in good standing in all appropriate professional and governmental organizations. Must be eligible to obtain and maintain active provider enrollment and credentialing with commercial, Medicare, and Medicaid insurance payers or ability to obtain within 60 days of hire. *To see the full job description go to Position Description at the bottom of this posting. Total Rewards: Our employees are what make DMU special, so we treat them well! Our Total Rewards reflect this commitment. Qualified faculty and staff enjoy a generous employer contribution towards the medical plan, 10% retirement match, flexible work arrangements, community service time, tuition assistance, professional development funding, and access to wellness facilities with programs that promote a well-balanced lifestyle. Visit www.dmu.edu/employment to learn more about our benefits. DMU is proud to offer employees generous benefits and perks, paid time off, free use of wellness facilities, and a host of employee engagement and recognition programs throughout the year. About: Founded in 1898, Des Moines University is a premier medical and health sciences institution comprising three colleges– College of Osteopathic Medicine, College of Podiatric Medicine and Surgery, and College of Health Sciences – offering ten graduate degree programs. Our mission is to improve lives in our global community by educating diverse groups of highly competent and compassionate health professionals. It is an exciting time to join DMU. In 2023, we relocated our primary academic and operational offices to a new 88-acre campus in West Des Moines, Iowa, while maintaining an active clinic on our former campus. This state-of-the-art campus includes technology-rich, flexible education spaces that support innovative teaching methods and connect faculty and students across all of our programs. Our new research facilities include a vibrant and spacious open laboratory, designed to foster collaboration and innovation. DMU enhances our community’s quality of life by educating outstanding health professionals and leaders; providing expert, compassionate patient care; serving the community in diverse ways; and stimulating the central Iowa community. At DMU you will make a meaningful contribution to the dynamic future of Medicine and Health Sciences by supporting a diverse community of faculty and staff with programs and services across the employee lifecycle. Required Documents: Resume, cover letter, and contact information for three professional references required at time of online submission. Apply at www.dmu.edu/employment. jobs.description: Job Search Subscribe to jobs Assistant Professor Anatomy Apply now Job no: 493016 Work type: FT Location: West Des Moines Categories: Faculty At Des Moines University Medicine and Health Sciences, you will make a meaningful contribution to the dynamic future of medicine and health sciences while helping shape the next generation of healthcare leaders. DMU is seeking an Anatomy Faculty Member who is passionate about teaching, discovery, and service. What you’ll do: In this role, you will play a vital part in delivering an exceptional educational experience while advancing scholarly work and contributing to the academic community. You will: Teach and/or coordinate courses within the prescribed curriculum, including engaging classroom and gross anatomy laboratory instruction Facilitate active learning through small-group experiences such as problem-based and case-based sessions Support student success through mentoring, advising, and maintaining regular office hours Design and implement effective instructional strategies, assessments, and innovative teaching approaches Develop and sustain an independent, externally funded research program Prepare and submit grant proposals and disseminate research through peer-reviewed publications Pursue ongoing professional development to stay at the forefront of anatomical sciences Actively contribute to departmental, university, and professional service, including governance and committee work Engage in community outreach and service initiatives that reflect DMU’s mission What we are looking for: We are seeking a collaborative educator and scholar who brings enthusiasm, expertise, and a commitment to student success. Ideal candidates will have: Earned doctoral degree (or willingness to complete one within an agreed timeframe) Strong communication and presentation skills Excellent organizational and time management abilities Proficiency with computer applications and the ability to integrate technology into teaching Commitment to and alignment with DMU’s mission and values. Preferred qualifications include: Demonstrated teaching experience in anatomical sciences A record of—or strong potential for—developing an externally funded research program Evidence of scholarly activity, including publications Ability or willingness to teach histology and/or neuroanatomy topics is preferred To see the full job description, please refer to the Position Description at the bottom of this posting. Total Rewards At DMU, we invest in our people because they are the foundation of our success. About Des Moines University Medicine and Health Sciences Founded in 1898, Des Moines University Medicine and Health Sciences is a premier institution with three colleges: the College of Osteopathic Medicine, the College of Podiatric Medicine and Surgery, and the College of Health Sciences. DMU offers a variety of graduate-level programs including anatomy, biomedical sciences, public health, physical therapy, physician assistant studies, and more. Located in West Des Moines, part of Iowa’s capital metro, DMU fosters a collaborative, student-centered environment where learners consistently exceed national benchmarks in board scores, certification pass rates, and residency placements. Our new 88-acre campus brings together cutting-edge technology, flexible learning environments, and modern research facilities designed to encourage collaboration, innovation, and discovery. Combined with clinical operations in downtown Des Moines, DMU is redefining how health sciences education is delivered. At DMU, you will be part of a mission-driven community dedicated to improving lives locally and globally through education, research, and service. jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Art Two-Year Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship (Start Fall 2026)
jobs.description: The Department of Art invites applications for a two-year Andrew W. Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship in Video production and Digital Media Fall 2026. Eligible candidates must have received their terminal PhD or MFA degree in 2023 or later.   The annual teaching load for the Mellon Fellow is two courses per year (one per semester). The Mellon Fellow will support both the Art Studio Major and the Film and Media Studies (FMS) concentration by teaching two FMS/ART video production courses in AY26–27 and two ART digital media studio courses in AY27–28. The FMS-255 Fundamentals of Video Production course is a FMS Concentration requirement, and will connect with a wide range of Majors/Concentrations across campus. The ART-246 level Digital Media course is an elective Studio Art major course that helps to fulfil the major's requirements. The Fellow will also be expected to share their research with the Grinnell community and to be a contributing member of the department.   Additional information about our curriculum and faculty can be found at Film and Media Studies Concentration: https://www.grinnell.edu/academics/majors concentrations/film - media and Studio Art Major: https://www.grinnell.edu/academics/majors concentrations/studio - art

jobs.description: The Department of German Studies invites applications for a 1-year term appointment with the possibility of renewal in any area of German Studies, beginning Fall 2026. Near-native fluency in German is required. Assistant Professor (Ph.D.) preferred; Instructor (ABD) or Associate Professor possible. Research and teaching interests might include but are not limited to: 20 th -21 st century German-language literature, film, visual culture, theater, or other media; interdisciplinary connections to African Diaspora Studies, Jewish Studies, Gender and Women’s studies, LGBTQ+ studies, (post)colonial studies, or a focus on other minoritized communities in the German-speaking world. The teaching load is five courses over two semesters.  Additional information about our curriculum and faculty can be found at HTTPS://WWW.GRINNELL.EDU/ACADEMICS/MAJORS-CONCENTRATIONS/GERMAN.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Neuroscience 2-Year Term (Start Fall 2026)
jobs.description: GRINNELL COLLEGE. The Neuroscience Program invites applications for a neuroscientist with a 2-year term contract, beginning Fall 2026. Assistant Professor (Ph.D.) preferred; Instructor (ABD) or Associate Professor possible. The teaching load of five courses over two semesters (with lab sections counting as ½ course) will include one or more courses in our neuroscience curriculum (Foundations of Neuroscience and/or Neuroscience Senior Seminar), with the remaining courses in either the biology or psychology departments, depending on the candidates’ interest/expertise . Term contract renewals are subject to departmental and college priorities and budget availability.   Additional information about our curriculum and faculty in Biology, Psychology and Neuroscience can be found at https://www.grinnell.edu/academics/majors-concentrations/   Complete applications, which include letters of recommendation, will be considered on a rolling basis. Regarding recommendation letters, note that once the applicant submits their portion of the application, the system will email requests for letters to reference providers indicated by the applicant in the application. The applicant will be able to track the submission status of these reference letters online.

jobs.description: Job Search Subscribe to jobs Assistant Professor Primary Care (.5 FTE) Apply now Job no: 493018 Work type: PT Location: West Des Moines Categories: Faculty Des Moines University Medicine and Health Sciences is seeking a passionate and collaborative Academic Internal Medicine Faculty Member to join our Primary Care–Academic Department in a part-time role averaging 20 hours per week (0.5 FTE). This is an exciting opportunity for a physician who is enthusiastic about medical education and committed to shaping the future of healthcare through innovation, mentorship, and student engagement. Reporting to the Chair of the Primary Care–Academic Department, this faculty member will play an integral role in delivering a dynamic and learner-centered educational experience. Working alongside a dedicated team of Primary Care faculty, the successful candidate will contribute to classroom instruction, develop and facilitate laboratories and clinical skills experiences, and support a variety of educational initiatives that advance the mission and priorities of both the department and the University. If you are energized by teaching, value academic collaboration, and enjoy inspiring learners as they prepare for careers in medicine, we invite you to bring your expertise and enthusiasm to DMU. What you’ll do: Deliver engaging medical education by planning, facilitating, and assessing a variety of learning experiences, including classroom lectures, small-group instruction, simulation activities, and clinical clerkship didactics across DMU's health sciences programs. Support curricular excellence and innovation through active participation in curriculum development, continuous improvement initiatives, student advising and mentorship, admissions interviews, and fostering an inclusive learning environment that promotes student success. Contribute to the University and broader community by serving on committees, supporting student organizations, participating in outreach efforts, completing required training, and collaborating on special projects that advance the mission of DMU and the profession. What we are looking for: D.O. degree from a COCA accredited college of osteopathic medicine or an M.D. degree from an LCME accredited college of medicine. Board-eligible/certified by the American Osteopathic Board of Internal Medicine or board eligible/certified by American Board of Internal Medicine. If board eligible, must obtain certification within one year of employment. The ideal candidate will possess a minimum of 3 years of full time clinical experience in Internal Medicine or a related fellowship trained clinical practice. *To see the full job description go to Position Description at the bottom of this posting. jobs.title: Clinical Associate/Assistant Professor Social Work
jobs.description: Faculty HomeMy Faculty JobsSearch Jobs CLINICAL ASSOCIATE/ASSISTANT PROFESSOR SOCIAL WORKRequisition # 75950Position BasicsType of PositionCLINICAL-TRACKAdvertising Ends on:Extended Until Position is FilledAdvertising Started on:Thursday, May 28th, 2026College:College of Liberal Arts & SciencesDepartment:Social WorkSalarySalary:CommensuratePosition DetailsFull/Part Time Status:Full TimePosition Description:CLINICAL ASSISTANT/ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR (Iowa City MSW Practicum Faculty) School of Social Work Iowa City, IA ANTICIPATED START DATE: AUGUST 1, 2026 (FLEXIBLE) The University of Iowa, School of Social Work seeks a full-time, 12-month, clinical assistant or associate professor to support student success when preparing for, entering, and completing social work practicum at the master’s level. This position involves teaching practicum content courses, assisting with training practicum students and supervisors, identification and development of new placement sites based on the needs of the program and students, and serving as the lead liaison to practicum sites. The individual should have social work practice experience and expertise to guide MSW students specializing in clinical or leadership practice in seeking practicum placements. The individual should also have experience teaching in social work, with the ability to teach in person and online. They should also be able to engage in professional productivity and service. This position is based in Iowa City. The initial appointment is for one year (2026-27), renewable for up to two years (2027-28) and 2028-29), and renewable thereafter in three-year increments, pending collegiate approval and demonstrated excellence in teaching. More information about the Clinical Track can be found on the Provost’s website at https://provost.uiowa.edu/human-resources-administration/faculty-hr-administration/faculty-appointment#clinical. The School of Social Work offers programs at the BA, MSW, and PhD levels with faculty scholarship foci in the areas of aging, child welfare, behavioral and mental health, and organizations and communities. In addition to programs on our main Iowa City campus, the School of Social Work maintains MSW programs in Des Moines, Sioux City, and an online program serving all of Iowa and surrounding states. For more information on the School’s many resources and programs, see our homepage at http://socialwork.uiowa.edu. (Requisition #75950) Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit their materials immediately, as application review will begin June 1, 2026. All materials must be submitted online at https://jobs.uiowa.edu/jobSearch/faculty/ . Refer to requisition number #75950. Do not mail paper applications. A curriculum vitae, letter of application describing your interest, preparation, and vision for social work practicum education and contact information for three references will need to be attached during the online application process. For inquiries about the position please contact the Search Committee Chair: Peggy L. Trosper, MSW, LMSW, Director of Practicum Education University of Iowa School of Social Work 308 North Hall, Iowa City, IA 52242 peggy-trosper@uiowa.edu WORK AUTHORIZATION INFORMATION For H-1B petitions subject to the September 19, 2025 Presidential Proclamation, please note that the department will not cover the $100,000 payment associated with H-1B sponsorship, either at the time of hire or for international travel purposes. We encourage impacted individuals to explore alternative pathways for work authorization. Our team is available to help identify options that may be suitable for your situation. MISCONDUCT DISCLOSURE Successful candidates will be required to self-disclose any misconduct history or pending research misconduct investigation including but not limited to sexual misconduct in prior employment and provide a related release and will be subject to a criminal background and credential check. Education Requirement: MSW from a CSWE accredited program. Required Qualifications: A minimum of three years post-graduate level practice experience. Demonstrated teaching experience in social work. Experience with practicum education (as practicum supervisor, liaison, or practicum seminar instructor) Current license at the Master’s level of social work (LMSW). Potential for professional productivity, practice, and service through such activities as CEU or conference presentations, professional consultation, outreach activities, publications, membership in state or regional boards or professional organizations. Desirable Qualifications: Knowledge of Council on Social Work Education (CSWE) Educational Policy and Academic Standards. LISW or equivalent clinical social work licensure in current state of residence/employment. Five or more years post-graduate level practice experience in clinical or leadership practice. Online Application Required Documents Curriculum VitaeLetter of InterestSupporting Attachments Number of References: 3 Letters of Recommendation are required as part of the application process.
